title: legal-redlines-scratchpad-julia-khan
content:
Quick scratchpad for upcoming partner MSA negotiation. Mostly talking points and clauses to watch - keep editable.

Context:
- Partner: DataViz.ai (pipeline/analytics startup). They want dedicated capacity + a hosted fallback.
- Commercial lead: Marcus. Target: 1yr commitment, pilot -> expand.
- Risk appetite: moderate. Need strong data protections + limitation on downstream use; push back on unlimited liability.

Top clauses to watch (priority order):
1) Data use / model training prohibition
   - Their redline: broad license to "use" Customer Data for service improvement. NO.
   - Our ask: explicit prohibition on using any customer-provided data to train models or improve models outside of the customer's tenancy.
   - Suggested language (fallback): "Provider will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve any models outside the environment dedicated to Customer, except with Customer's prior written consent."
   - Negotiation point: Offer aggregated, anonymized telemetry (metrics only) as alternative.

2) PII / Sensitive Data and Security Controls
   - Look for: definitions that try to label all data as non-PII. Push clear examples: PHI, financial data, government IDs, etc.
   - Ask for: SOC2-equivalent controls, KMS integration, ability to specify that keys are customer-managed for dedicated/private deployments.
   - Audit clause: limit frequency and scope. We can support "reasonable" audits with redaction and mutual NDA; no continuous monitoring requests.

3) Liability cap & consequential damages
   - Their redline: no cap or cap equal to fees. Red flag.
   - Our position: cap = greater of 12 months' fees or $1M (commercial to decide), no consequential or punitive damages, carve-outs for willful misconduct and gross negligence.
   - Watch for indemnity drags (broad IP indemnities or product liability). Carve out model hallucination-type claims from indemnity whenever possible.

4) Availability / SLA and credits
   - They want 99.99% SLA for all endpoints including heavy batch jobs. Clarify different SLAs for hosted vs. dedicated vs. private.
   - We propose: 99.9% for hosted API, higher for dedicated with committed capacity, different measurement windows. Credits capped and not a termination right unless repeated breaches.

5) Termination and data return/secure deletion
   - Ensure clear timelines: data return within 30 days, secure deletion within 60 days. For on-prem/VPC, confirm operational steps (certified deletion, decommission checklist).
   - Contract should require us to provide export in standard formats (JSON/CSV) and provide certificate of deletion on request.

6) Export controls and sanctions
   - Confirm representations about compliance with US export controls and sanctions. Add right to suspend service for sanctioned activity.

7) Subprocessors / subcontractors / hosting locations
   - For Hosted: list major cloud providers, allow reasonable changes if notice + opt-out for sensitive customers (migration to private).
   - For Dedicated/Private: clarify that we are not going to route/split customer traffic through 3rd party without consent.

8) Confidentiality definition & residuals
   - Resist overly broad "residuals" language that prevents our engineers from using general know-how. Keep typical carve-outs for general knowledge and residuals with no micro-level data retention.

9) IP ownership & output rights
   - Clarify: Customer owns their data and any prompts they submit; provider owns the underlying service and model. For generated outputs, prefer customer ownership or at least a license back to customer for their use-case (avoid us asserting ownership of outputs).

10) Insurance
   - Ask for cyber liability + E&O. Typical req: $2M- $5M depending on customer size. Work with insurance to confirm provider coverage is acceptable.

Negotiation playbook / talking points (for Marcus + Aisha):
- Data training prohibition: high priority. Offer: telemetry + aggregated metrics; if they insist, offer opt-in with higher fee and strict scoping + audit rights.
- Liability cap: frame as standard market practice; show benchmarking (competitors X/Y use 12mo fees). If they push, give limited exceptions only for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
- SLAs: separate tiers - avoid single SLA across all products. Explain technical reasons (batch jobs have different availability profile).
- Subprocessors: agree to list and notify; offer quarterly summary of locations. For very sensitive customers, offer private deployment route.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm commercial cap target with finance (Connor). I think we can accept 12 months revenue or $1.5M - confirm risk tolerance.
- Check with infra whether we can provide cert-of-deletion for private deployments (Marcus to sync with infra).
- Ask engineering: can we limit telemetry to aggregated metrics only (no raw prompts) without breaking internal monitoring? (Aisha follow-up)
- Check precedent: search Conf:CONF-3982 for last MSA language around model training.

Draft redline snippets to copy into contract reviewer tool:
- "Provider will not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning model used outside the Customer's dedicated environment without Customer's prior written consent."
- "Customer Data means any data, including prompts and outputs, submitted to the Service by or on behalf of Customer in connection with the Agreement."
- "Upon termination, Provider shall securely delete all Customer Data from Provider systems within sixty (60) days and provide written certification of such deletion upon Customer's reasonable request."

Risks / negotiation traps we've seen:
- Customer attempts to frame "service improvement" as necessary for stability - call out narrow allowed telemetry only and require anonymization + aggregation.
- Broad "derivative works" claims to outputs - clarify ownership of outputs and grant narrow license for provider to use outputs only for debugging and service support, with no training rights.
- Indemnity tied to third-party claims for model outputs (e.g., hallucination leading to defamation suits). Try to limit indemnity to IP infringement and gross misconduct.

Notes to self / meeting prep (30 min call with DataViz.ai reps):
- Ask about their data classification - will they send PHI? If yes, need to route to Private + separate SOW.
- Confirm expected QPS and burst patterns; this informs SLA and pricing.
- Walk them through our telemetry/metrics offering as an alternative to training.
- Agree on pilot success criteria (latency < 150ms p50 for interactive, throughput X for batch).

End of scratchpad. Keep this doc mutable - will paste into PRD/Confluence later once language is stabilized.

Quick revision history: 2025-11-12 initial notes; 2026-01-10 added liability cap suggestions; 2026-02-20 updated data deletion timeline and audit fallback.
